title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy (likely a Mo–Nb–Ta–W–V system) produced by arc melting and drop casting into bulk BCC samples
recollection.intervention: Post-solidification thermal annealing at high temperature (around 1000–1200 °C) followed by controlled cooling to induce chemical short-range order (SRO)
recollection.structure: Body-centered cubic matrix with locally ordered atomic clusters (short-range ordered domains) embedded in a random solid solution
recollection.mechanism: Formation of chemical SRO reduces local mass and force-constant fluctuations, lowering phonon scattering rates and thereby enhancing coherent phonon transport
recollection.results: Room-temperature phonon heat conductivity increased by ~25–35% (e.g., from ~10 W/m·K in the random alloy to ~13–14 W/m·K in the SRO alloy)

score.note: The recollection correctly associates induced SRO with increased phonon conductivity but invents thermal annealing rather than Monte Carlo-controlled SRO. It gives only a generic BCC matrix with ordered clusters, missing the specific B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolative pathways. The reduced-scattering mechanism is directionally related but misstates the details and omits the key percolation and lattice-distortion effects. The claimed 25–35% increase is far from the actual ~12%.
